newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila Central Bank rate cut pulls down rates.
newsitem.headline: Manila Central Bank rate cut pulls down rates.

text.p: Philippine overnight and term rates declined on Thursday in line with the across-the-board reduction in the Central Bank's benchmark rates, traders said.
The Central Bank earlier cut its overnight and term reverse repo rates after the peso appreciated steadily in recent days.
The interbank call rate fell to 14.03125 percent from Wednesday's 16.03125 percent, with a moderate turnover of 17.635 billion pesos.
"As expected, all banks just followed the overnight rate of the Central Bank," one trader said.
The Central Bank cut its overnight borrowing rate to 14 percent from 16 percent.

The trader said the turnover in the interbank market was slightly bloated due to the heavy borrowings of small banks after remitting corporate taxes estimated at between five billion to six billion pesos earlier this week.
"The bigger banks were able to cover their demand," the trader added.
Done rates ranged from 14.03125 percent to 14.25 percent.
The secondary Treasury bill market was also active with buyers on the look-out for longer-term bills.
"They are anticipating bill rates to go down further, especially in July when the next reserve cut takes effect," another trader said.
The Central Bank is scheduled to cut banks' reserve requirement by another one percentage point to 13 percent beginning July 4. It is expected to release six to seven billion pesos to the market.
Bids for one-year bills ranged from 11.25 to 11.375 percent, while offers ranged from 11.15 to 11.20 percent. The rates were lower than the average 364-day auction rate of 11.375 percent.
